leftEvidence.title: Mark preserves dazzling clothes and Peter’s fear

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: After six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them.
points.right: Jesus finds a crowd and scribes around the disciples; a father describes a destructive spirit and asks for help if Jesus can do anything.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Elijah and Moses appear speaking with Jesus; Peter proposes tents because he does not know what to say, a cloud overshadows them, and the voice commands listening.
points.right: Jesus redirects the “if,” the father answers with belief and unbelief, the boy is restored, prayer is named, and another death prediction leaves the disciples afraid to ask.

payload.posture: Mark joins frightened witnesses, public dispute, a father’s mixed belief, private prayer instruction, and another passion prediction.

rightEvidence.role: From glory into distress and another death prediction
rightEvidence.title: Mark expands the father’s struggle and the disciples’ failure

payload.tension: The two scenes preserve different forms of fear, uncertainty, and failed understanding.
payload.title: Terror on the mountain and contested belief below
